text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.83% today, a modest gain that comes after the stock had fallen 8.36% over the past two weeks. The immediate backdrop is shifting oil-market sentiment: Brent crude briefly dipped below $90 a barrel on November 10th following President Trump's comments that he expects the Iran conflict to end "fairly soon," which would reduce geopolitical risk premium in oil prices. US crude is currently trading at $99.64 per barrel, down from where it was during the earlier part of this two-week slide.

The broader context is that energy stocks like ConocoPhillips are caught between competing forces—lower oil prices (which hurt profitability) and reduced geopolitical tension (which the market sees as positive for stability and demand). The company reported earnings on November 5th, but the stock's steep two-week decline suggests that recent oil-price weakness and the de-escalation narrative have outweighed any positive earnings news so far.
